10/22/26  2:20 pm
Commenter: Commenter A, Southside Behavioral Health

Comments on CPST
 

Southside Behavioral Health (SBH) supports expanding access to community-based behavioral health services that promote recovery, strengthen natural supports, and help individuals function successfully in their homes and communities. The proposed Community Psychiatric Support and Treatment (CPST) model offers opportunities to provide individualized treatment and rehabilitation to adults, children, and families.

SBH serves Halifax, Mecklenburg, and Brunswick counties in rural Virginia. Our agency provides outpatient treatment, psychiatric services, case management, psychosocial rehabilitation, and crisis services, among other programs. Implementation of CPST must account for the circumstances of rural communities, including travel distances, transportation barriers, limited workforce availability, and uneven access to reliable internet and cellular service.

We respectfully request revisions and coordinated implementation guidance to ensure that the new requirements expand access without making services financially or operationally unsustainable for rural providers.

11/12/26  9:22 am
Commenter: Rappahannock Area Community Services Board

General Comments and Position
 

We appreciate the opportunity to provide comments regarding the proposed Community Psychiatric Support and Treatment (CPST) service and the associated changes to Virginia's behavioral health service delivery system.

We recognize the potential benefits of establishing CPST as a comprehensive, team-based service that integrates clinical interventions, crisis support, counseling, restorative evidence-based practices, care coordination, and individualized rehabilitation supports. The proposed model offers opportunities to provide more coordinated and clinically responsive services to adults and youth in their homes and communities.  However, it does not serve as a viable replacement for legacy services.

However, significant concerns remain regarding the practical feasibility, financial sustainability, workforce requirements, and potential impact on individuals who currently rely on existing behavioral health services.

11/12/26  1:57 pm
Commenter: Virginia Association of Community Based Providers

VACBP Comments on CPST Emergency Regulations (12VAC35-105-1420 through 1425)
 

On behalf of the Virginia Association of Community-Based Providers (VACBP), thank you for the opportunity to comment on the emergency regulations establishing licensing requirements for Community Psychiatric Support and Treatment (CPST).

VACBP represents community-based behavioral health providers across the Commonwealth. Our members provide the services that behavioral health redesign is creating, and they must meet both DBHDS licensing regulations and DMAS Medicaid requirements. Where the two sets of rules differ, providers have to track two standards, and they risk receiving inconsistent findings in licensing reviews and Medicaid audits. VACBP's Member's Advisory Council reviewed these regulations on October 8, 2026, and these comments reflect that discussion.

VACBP supports DBHDS's goal of licensing CPST as a team-based service that restores functioning and helps adults and youth succeed at home, at school, at work, and in the community. Our comments focus on clarifying requirements and aligning them with the DMAS CPST policy (draft dated June 8, 2026), which will protect access and reduce the burden of complying with two standards.
